name: Documenso
description: Send documents for signature and keep the signed copies, with a private PostgreSQL database, a generated signing certificate, and a preconfigured administrator.

services.name: documenso
commandArgv: CERT=/home/nodejs/cert.p12; if [ ! -f "$CERT" ]; then openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -keyout /tmp/k.pem -out /tmp/c.pem -days 3650 -subj "/CN=Documenso" 2>/dev/null && openssl pkcs12 -export -out "$CERT" -inkey /tmp/k.pem -in /tmp/c.pem -passout env:NEXT_PRIVATE_SIGNING_PASSPHRASE && rm -f /tmp/k.pem /tmp/c.pem; fi; exec sh start.sh

configFields.label: Session signing secret
configFields.help: Auto-generated. Signs sign-in sessions; changing it signs everyone out.

configFields.label: Encryption key
configFields.help: Auto-generated. Encrypts sensitive values stored in the database; losing it makes them unreadable.

configFields.label: Secondary encryption key
configFields.help: Auto-generated. A second key Documenso requires alongside the primary one.

configFields.label: Signing certificate passphrase
configFields.help: Auto-generated. Protects the self-signed certificate created on first start and stored on the persistent volume.

fields.label: Admin email
fields.help: Used for the initial administrator. Manage existing accounts in the app.

settings.label: Outgoing email
settings.description: Documenso emails signing requests and notifications, so it needs an SMTP server.

fields.label: SMTP username
fields.help: Leave empty for a relay that needs no login.

fields.label: Use TLS from the start
fields.help: Turn on for port 465. Leave off for port 587, which upgrades with STARTTLS.

fields.label: From address
fields.help: The sender shown on signing requests.

fields.label: Disable public sign-ups
fields.help: Sign-ups are open by default, as in upstream. Turn this on once you have invited the people you need; the administrator account already exists.

prepare.title: Create the administrator
prepare.description: Creates the administrator through Documenso's own sign-up, then marks it verified and gives it the admin role.
prepare.command: cd /app/apps/remix && node -e 'const b=process.env.NEXT_PRIVATE_INTERNAL_WEBAPP_URL,o=process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_WEBAPP_URL;fetch(b+"/api/auth/email-password/signup",{method:"POST",headers:{"content-type":"application/json",origin:o},body:JSON.stringify({name:process.env.ADMIN_NAME,email:process.env.ADMIN_EMAIL,password:process.env.ADMIN_PASSWORD})}).then(async r=>{const t=await r.text();console.log("signup",r.status,t.slice(0,120));process.exit(r.status===201?0:1)}).catch(e=>{console.log("signup failed",e.message);process.exit(1)})' && E=$(printf %s "$ADMIN_EMAIL" | sed "s/'/''/g") && echo "UPDATE \"User\" SET \"emailVerified\" = now(), roles = ARRAY['USER','ADMIN']::\"Role\"[] WHERE lower(email) = lower('$E');" | npx prisma db execute --stdin --schema ../../packages/prisma/schema.prisma

connection.title: Sign in to Documenso
connection.description: Sign in with the email and generated password below. The administrator account is created and verified on first start, so no confirmation email is needed.

firstLogin.note: Account changes made in the app (a password change, new users) are preserved on redeployment. Public sign-ups are open until you turn them off in settings. Documents are signed with a self-signed certificate generated on first start and kept on the persistent volume; add a trusted certificate if recipients need to see a verified signer.

features.title: Document signing
features.description: Send documents for signature and keep the signed copies.

features.title: Private database
features.description: Documents and accounts live in a dedicated, project-scoped Postgres instance.

features.title: Ready to sign
features.description: A signing certificate and the administrator are created for you on first start.
